title: How to Block Notifications from One Website in Chrome
description: Stop unwanted website notifications in desktop Chrome while keeping useful alerts. Learn why blocking pop-ups does not also block notifications.

sections.heading: Check whether the message is a notification or a pop-up
paragraphs: If messages keep appearing after you block pop-ups, check the website's notification permission. Google treats these as separate controls: stopping new windows or tabs does not necessarily stop alerts from a site you previously allowed.

To silence one website while keeping email or meeting alerts, change that site's permission first. This guide covers desktop Chrome. The official instructions linked below were checked on October 17, 2026.

sections.heading: Block the website from Chrome settings
paragraphs: Read the website address shown on the unwanted notification, then open Chrome settings yourself. You do not need to follow an unfamiliar notification's link to reach these controls.
bullets: Open the three-dot menu in Chrome's upper-right corner and choose Settings.
Go to Privacy and security, then Site settings, then Notifications.
Find the Not allowed to send notifications list and choose Add.
Enter the address of the website you want to silence and confirm with Add.

sections.heading: Why the pop-up blocker did not stop the alerts
paragraphs: A pop-up opens browser content in a window or tab. A website notification uses a permission you can manage separately. Check the type of interruption before choosing which setting to change.
If a page launches a new window, inspect Pop-ups and redirects. If an allowed website repeatedly sends notification messages, inspect Notifications. When both happen, review both permissions.

sections.heading: Review existing permissions after changing the default
paragraphs: Chrome lets individual websites use their own permissions instead of the default. After changing the general notification setting, also review the sites you previously allowed.
Quieter messaging changes how a website asks for permission. It should not be treated as a switch that revokes every notification permission already granted.

sections.heading: Check the sender if another alert appears
paragraphs: After blocking a site, check whether new messages actually come from that address. An alert from another site does not establish that the block failed.
bullets: Compare the sender address on the new notification with the address you blocked.
If new tabs keep opening, the homepage changes unexpectedly, or unfamiliar extensions appear, Google's unwanted-software guidance may be more relevant than notification settings alone.

sections.heading: If an alert asks you to scan or download something
paragraphs: Do not follow a suspicious update or download prompt. Visit the software provider's official website directly when you need a download. Blocking a notification sender does not scan your computer or remove software already installed.
This article is based on official documentation. The steps have not been independently reproduced on a physical PC. Menu placement can vary with the Chrome version and interface language.
